title: Pump prices seen going down by P3 per liter
summary: Gasoline and diesel prices could be headed for another rollback next week, with industry projections of P3 to P3.50 per liter decrease for both following four days of trading in the Mean of Platts…

blocks.text: Oil prices remained relatively low this week amid expectations of a supply surplus following increased crude loadings from Middle Eastern terminals outside the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

MANILA, Philippines — Gasoline and diesel prices could be headed for another rollback next week, with industry projections of P3 to P3.50 per liter decrease for both following four days of trading in the Mean of Platts Singapore.

Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said the development overshadowed concerns over shipping risks as attacks in the narrow waterway, which typically handles about 20 percent of global oil and gas supplies, continued.
“Product prices also eased further this week, as strong supply outlook amid rising Chinese exports continues to loosen tight availability of both gasoline and diesel in the region,” Bellas said.
He, however, warned that continued attacks on shipping vessels in the Strait of Hormuz could have an immediate impact on oil supplies from the Middle East.
With one trading day remaining, the projected price reductions may still increase or decrease. If implemented, next week’s rollback would mark the fourth straight week of cuts.
The Department of Energy is expected to announce the prescribed price adjustments on Monday that will take effect the following day.

Meanwhile, state-run Philippine National Oil Co. (PNOC) continues to advance the establishment of the government-maintained strategic petroleum reserve (SPR), which President Marcos described as a national priority.

“For the Philippines, our priority is clear: we are advancing our (SPR), backed by the robust infrastructure and financing required to sustain it,” Marcos said during the 4th Asia Zero-Emission Community Leaders’ Meeting in Manila.
The SPR, which will be located at the PNOC Industrial Park in Mariveles, Bataan, targets a total storage capacity of 15 million barrels of diesel, enough to cover about 75 days of demand.
The project’s initial phase involves the construction of six large storage tanks with a combined capacity of one million barrels. The first tank is targeted for completion by the end of 2027.
The remaining 14 million barrels of storage capacity, meanwhile, will be built through public-private partnerships and consortium arrangements.
